## Key Files Explained

### 1. README.md (17,000+ bytes)
- Design philosophy: "alive" server with AI consciousness
- Architecture diagram (5 layers)
- Comparison with desktop edition
- 5 deployment targets (home, business, cloud, edge, homelab)
- Sentinel AI core components (5 subsystems)
- Security architecture (zero-trust)
- Quick start commands
- Performance targets

### 2. kernel-ai/kirat-ai.c (20,000+ bytes)
- **Purpose**: Kernel module bridging Linux kernel ↔ AI runtime
- **Interfaces**:
  - `/dev/kirat-ai` — character device (commands via ioctl/write)
  - `/sys/kernel/kirat/` — sysfs (configuration)
  - Netlink protocol 31 — async kernel events to userspace
- **Capabilities**:
  - Real-time system telemetry (CPU, memory, I/O, thermal, power)
  - eBPF program injection for custom tracing
  - Process priority boosting (SCHED_FIFO)
  - CPU isolation (affinity masks)
  - CPU governor control (performance/powersave/schedutil)
  - Memory reclaim triggering
- **Commands**:
  - `KIRAT_CMD_GET_SNAPSHOT` — immediate system state
  - `KIRAT_CMD_BOOST_PID` — boost process priority
  - `KIRAT_CMD_ISOLATE_PID` — isolate to specific CPUs
  - `KIRAT_CMD_SET_GOVERNOR` — change CPU governor
  - `KIRAT_CMD_FORCE_GC` — trigger memory reclaim

### 3. sentinel-core/README.md (14,000+ bytes)
- **Observability**: Collects 847+ metrics every 10 seconds
- **Anomaly Detection**: Statistical, multivariate, sequence-based
- **Forecasting**: Predicts failures before they happen
- **Self-Healing**: Auto-restart, clean temp, kill leaks, block IPs
- **Natural Language**: Conversational system management
  - Example: `"Why is database slow?"` → analyzes, diagnoses, proposes fix
- **Configuration**: Full YAML schema for rules, alerting, auto-healing
- **API**: REST + WebSocket + gRPC interfaces

### 4. scripts/build-server.sh (25,000+ bytes)
- **Purpose**: Automated server OS installation
- **Targets**: home-server, cloud, edge, homelab, database
- **Process**:
  1. Disk partitioning (GPT: EFI, boot, root, data)
  2. Base system (debootstrap Debian)
  3. System configuration (network, SSH, users)
  4. Kernel optimization (sysctl, CPU governor, IRQ affinity)
  5. Sentinel AI installation (kernel module, Python service)
  6. Workload installation (Docker-based services)
  7. Bootloader (systemd-boot)
  8. First-boot interactive setup
- **Security**: No root SSH, key-only auth, hardened SSH config
- **Profiles**: Each target pre-installs relevant services

### 5. scripts/vm-server.sh (13,000+ bytes)
- **Purpose**: Safe VM testing + cloud deployment
- **VM Commands**:
  - `create-vm` — create QCOW2 disk
  - `test-install <iso>` — test OS installation in VM
  - `boot` — boot with GUI (for interactive testing)
  - `boot-headless` — background VM (SSH only)
  - `ssh` — SSH into VM (port 2222 forwarded)
- **Cloud Deploy**:
  - `deploy-hetzner` — Hetzner Cloud API
  - `deploy-aws` — AWS EC2 API
  - `deploy-do` — DigitalOcean API
- **Cloud-init**: Auto-generates template for cloud providers

## Deployment Targets

| Target | Hardware | Use Case | Pre-installed |
|--------|----------|----------|---------------|
| home-server | Old PC, NUC, Pi | Media, files, home automation | Jellyfin, Nextcloud, Pi-hole, WireGuard |
| cloud | VPS, EC2, Hetzner | Web hosting, APIs, staging | Nginx, K3s, PostgreSQL, Redis |
| edge | Industrial PC, Jetson | Factory, retail, agriculture | MQTT, SQLite, TensorFlow Lite |
| homelab | Pi cluster, VM farm | K8s learning, distributed systems | K3s, Nomad, Consul, Vault |
| database | Dedicated server | High-performance databases | PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse, Patroni |

## Quick Start Commands

```bash
# 1. Build server ISO (on a Linux machine)
sudo ./scripts/build-server.sh \
    --target home-server \
    --hostname mediahub \
    --disk /dev/sda

# 2. Test in VM first (safe!)
./scripts/vm-server.sh create-vm
./scripts/vm-server.sh test-install kirat-os-server.iso

# 3. Boot and test
./scripts/vm-server.sh boot-headless
./scripts/vm-server.sh ssh

# 4. Deploy to cloud
export HETZNER_API_TOKEN="your-token"
./scripts/vm-server.sh deploy-hetzner cx31
```

## Comparison with Desktop Edition

| Feature | Desktop | Server (Sentinel) |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| Display | Wayland compositor | None (headless) |
| Primary Access | Local KB/mouse | SSH, API, WebSocket |
| AI Focus | Chat, code help | System ops, monitoring, security |
| Kernel | Standard preempt | Real-time + eBPF heavy |
| Storage | XFS/ext4 | ZFS/Ceph/NVMe-oF |
| Networking | Standard | DPDK/XDP/WireGuard mesh |
| Workloads | Single-user apps | Containers, K8s, databases |
| Power | Performance | Efficiency + thermal-aware |
| Management | Manual | Fully automated + AI-driven |

## Teacher's Notes

- This is a **server-optimized redesign** of the original KIRAT OS desktop concept
- The kernel module (`kirat-ai.ko`) is the key differentiator — direct kernel-AI bridge
- Sentinel AI is designed to be **proactive**, not just reactive
- All workloads run in **Docker containers** for isolation and easy management
- **Cloud-init** enables one-command deployment to any cloud provider
- The build script uses **debootstrap** for speed; LFS-from-scratch is still possible but takes 8+ hours
- **Security is default-deny**: no passwords, no root SSH, mTLS everywhere
